title: What Counts from an Out-of-Network Fill on a Ridgecrest RxSecure Enrollment
content:
What counts from a fill dispensed by an out-of-network pharmacy toward an out-of-pocket total on a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan is worked out from the plan's own negotiated price on such fills, and which price is taken turns on the number of fills standing paid for the contract year. The plan treats 4 or more fills standing paid as a long fill history.

1. Where a fill dispensed by an out-of-network pharmacy stands on the pharmacy record and the member's fills standing paid for the contract year are 4 or more, what counts from such a fill is worked out as the largest plan negotiated price recorded on one of them.
2. Where a fill dispensed by an out-of-network pharmacy stands on the pharmacy record and the member's fills standing paid are fewer than 4, what counts from such a fill is worked out as the plan negotiated price recorded on the latest of them.
3. Where no fill dispensed by an out-of-network pharmacy stands on the pharmacy record, nothing counts from such a fill.

| A fill dispensed out of network stands on the record | Fills standing paid for the contract year | What counts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | 4 or more | the largest plan negotiated price recorded on such a fill |
| yes | fewer than 4 | the plan negotiated price recorded on the latest such fill |
| no | any | nothing |

What the member handed over at such a pharmacy above the plan's negotiated price for the fill never counts.

## Worked on a hypothetical record

Take a record carrying two fills dispensed out of network, the earlier at a plan negotiated price of 260.00 USD and the later at 145.00 USD, on which the member handed over 300.00 USD at the later pharmacy.

- With 5 fills standing paid for the contract year: 260.00 USD counts, being the largest plan negotiated price recorded on an out-of-network fill.
- With 3 fills standing paid: 145.00 USD counts, being the price recorded on the latest of them.
- In neither case does any part of the 300.00 USD above the plan's negotiated price count.
